Miami-Dade woke up to spotty showers blowing across the area on Tuesday morning, paired with a welcome taste of fall. Early morning temperatures dipped into the low to mid-70s before warming toward the mid-80s for the afternoon.

Blustery winds building between 25 and 30 mph are creating hazardous coastal conditions. A dangerous high risk of rip currents is active along Atlantic beaches through Friday, alongside a small craft advisory for Atlantic and Keys waters.

Wednesday will bring even cooler inland morning lows in the upper 60s, while coastal areas stay in the low 70s. After low 80s daytime highs and lighter winds mid-week, rain chances surge late week with scattered thunderstorms arriving for the weekend.

draft.article: Miami-Dade County residents can now cast their ballots early. Early voting began on Monday, Oct. 19, and continues through Nov. 1. Voting runs daily from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. at designated sites where voters can also drop off ballots. Anyone planning to vote, whether during the early voting window or on election day, must bring a valid photo ID featuring a signature.

headlines: MIAMI-DADE FIREFIGHTERS TACKLE EARLY MORNING TRAILER AND TRUCK FIRE ON NW 79TH
MASSIVE FLAMES ENGULF TRAILER IN NORTHWEST MIAMI-DADE
HOW MIAMI-DADE CREWS STOPPED A 3 A.M. BLAZE FROM SPREADING
draft.article: Miami-Dade Fire Rescue teams tackled a dangerous fire early Tuesday morning in northwest Miami-Dade. Crews were dispatched around 3:21 a.m. to the 1200 block of Northwest 79th Street, sending 10 units to the scene. First responders arrived to discover a converted trailer and a box truck completely covered in flames. Firefighters quickly rolled out hose lines to confront the blaze. Their fast action successfully kept the flames from catching onto other vehicles parked nearby. Once the main fire was extinguished, crews sprayed specialized firefighting foam across the site to keep hot spots from reigniting. Officials reported no injuries, and an investigation into the cause is ongoing.

headlines: HIALEAH POLICE WARN OF SCAMMERS POSING AS OFFICERS TO DEMAND CASH
BEWARE OF FAKE POLICE PHONE CALLS TARGETING HIALEAH RESIDENTS
HIALEAH RESIDENTS URGED TO HANG UP ON SUSPICIOUS POLICE CALLS
draft.article: The Hialeah Police Department is alerting the community after scammers posing as law enforcement officers began targeting local residents over the phone. Fraudsters are telling people that they have outstanding warrants, pending cases, or unpaid bonds, and they are demanding payments. Authorities note that these callers sometimes use actual officer names, real badge numbers, and spoofed caller ID details to deceive targets. Officials emphasize that police will never contact anyone by phone to demand money to avoid an arrest. Anyone receiving such a call should hang up immediately and report the incident to Hialeah police at 305-687-2525.

items.desc: Mosquitoes remain active in Miami-Dade through fall. Learn how to reduce bites and breeding areas as the county responds to locally transmitted dengue cases.

headlines: MIAMI-DADE ISSUES MOSQUITO ALERT AFTER LOCAL DENGUE CASES CONFIRMED
DRAIN STANDING WATER AS MIAMI FIGHTS FALL MOSQUITOES
WHY MIAMI-DADE TEAMS NEVER STOP TARGETING BREEDING SITES THIS FALL
draft.article:
Miami-Dade County remains under a mosquito-borne illness alert following confirmed local dengue transmissions this fall. Even as rain decreases and temperatures cool, local mosquito activity continues across the area.

In response, the Mosquito Control Division of the Department of Solid Waste Management is deploying truck spray treatments using Bti larvicide alongside adult mosquito spraying. County technicians monitor more than 350 traps every week, while partnering with the Florida Department of Health, the University of Florida, and Florida International University on viral tracking and testing.

Officials urge residents to empty standing water, as species such as Aedes aegypti require only one ounce of water to breed. Property inspections can be requested by calling 311.

headlines: DADE COUNTY WAS OFFICIALLY CREATED ON FEBRUARY 4, 1836
DADE COUNTY AND FORT DALLAS FOUNDED IN 1836
REMEMBERING THE 1836 CREATION OF DADE COUNTY AND FORT DALLAS
draft.article: Our local area marked a major milestone on February 4, 1836, when Dade County was officially created. The newly formed county was named after Major Francis L. Dade and the Miami River. The year 1836 also marked the construction of Fort Dallas. Once built, Fort Dallas served as a military base during the Second Seminole War, making 1836 a defining year for the establishment of Dade County, the Miami River territory, and the military post.
